Date: 2026-09-21
Time: 15:00 - 15:45 UTC
Duration: 45 min
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Sofia Martinez (Redwood SE), Avery Kim (Redwood Product), Ben Carter (Atlas Health CTO), Maya Singh (Platform Eng), Liam O'Connor (SRE), Priya Verma (Security)
Recording: cloud
Notes: demo/walkthrough focused on Console tracing, error analysis, request logs and debugging flows.
summary: Redwood performed a console walkthrough focused on tracing, error analysis, and request logs for Atlas Health. Customer is evaluating hosted vs dedicated and an on-prem pilot for PII-sensitive workloads. Key asks: SOC2/security docs, sample request logs export, benchmark of request-log ingestion/trace query latency, and pricing for a 3-month pilot. Agreed next steps and owners.
topics: Error analysis and root cause drill-down
Debugging flow with request -> trace correlation
Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private considerations
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll run through the Redwood Console tracing, error analysis, and how request logs tie into debugging flows. I'm jordan, AE for the account.
[00:08] Ben Carter: hey jordan, thanks, we got about 45 minutes. we'll try to cover the security bits early.
[00:15] Sofia Martinez: quick intro, i'm sofia, i'll demo the console, open up the tracing tab. if you see any questions just interrupt.
[00:23] Maya Singh: sounds good, our priorities are latency troubleshooting, being able to link user requests to traces, and data residency.
[00:30] Jordan Lee: perfect. so quick context — atlas runs inference across a mix of hosted and on-prem, right? maya correct?
[00:38] Maya Singh: yes we have a prod hosted flow for lower-risk stuff, but we want private for PII workflows.
[00:45] Sofia Martinez: okay i'm sharing my screen, loading the Console. top nav, tracing, request logs, error analysis tabs. we'll start with a sample trace.
[00:55] [screen share sound] Sofia Martinez: here you can see a trace timeline, spans for routing, model selection, kv cache hit, tokenization, generation. note the span durations — redwood automatically surfaces slow spans.
[01:10] Liam O'Connor: quick q — is kv-cache shown as one span or per layer?
[01:16] Sofia Martinez: it's grouped as kv-cache in this trace but you can expand per layer, the ui will sometimes collapse similar spans and label it kv-cache or kv cache depending on model.
[01:28] Ben Carter: that's helpful. can we search traces by request id from our logs?
[01:33] Sofia Martinez: yes — that's the main debugging flow. request logs have a request_id field that maps to trace_id. i'll demo searching for a request id from a sample request log.
[01:42] Sofia Martinez: typing... here's the request log entry, status 500, error.code=MODEL_TIMEOUT, payload size 12kb. clicking 'open trace' loads the full trace.
[01:52] [audio glitch] Speaker 1: so if you open the trace you'll see the model timeout span at 1.2s in the generation stage, and an upstream routing retry that added latency.
[02:05] Maya Singh: are request logs forwarded to our S3 or do we query via console?
[02:10] Jordan Lee: both options: Console for interactive debugging; we can also configure export to your S3 or GCS bucket. exports are gzipped ndjson, includes request_id, model, route, tokens, prompt hashes (we can redact prompt content on export).
[02:26] Priya Verma: on redaction — will exported logs still contain PII or PHI? we need assurances.
[02:32] Sofia Martinez: exports can be configured to mask or completely omit prompt and user_text fields. for PHI/PII sensitive flows we'd recommend Private deployment with customer KMS and on-prem export.
[02:44] Ben Carter: great. what's the latency for trace queries? if we have 10k traces/day will queries be interactive?
[02:52] Sofia Martinez: typical interactive is sub-second for recent traces; for volume we index key fields and you can pre-aggregate. for very high ingestion we recommend dedicated ingestion pipeline or retention tiering — i can share benchmark numbers.
[03:07] Liam O'Connor: does the Console show token-level timings to debug slow generations?
[03:12] Sofia Martinez: yes we surface token generation timings and prompt vs generation split; sometimes the ui summaries say e.g., generation dominated and you can click token heatmap.
[03:21] [short crosstalk] Ben Carter: okay show us error analysis.
[03:24] Sofia Martinez: switching to Error Analysis tab — we have grouped error types, the ability to drill into examples, and link back to traces and request logs. here's a cluster of model timeouts. clicking one opens a sample request and the trace.
[03:38] Maya Singh: can we run a bulk run across a test set to see regression before rollout?
[03:43] Avery Kim: yep — Redwood Optimize integrates with console to run evals against a benchmark set and surface regression alerts. we can hook your test prompts and run periodic checks.
[03:53] Ben Carter: good, we need that for compliance.
[03:56] Jordan Lee: quick note on routing — Console shows which model variant served the request and fallback history, so you can see if a cheaper quantized variant was used in fallback.
[04:08] Maya Singh: and how are rollouts represented?
[04:11] Sofia Martinez: rollouts show percent traffic, canary groups, and per-route latency and error deltas. very useful for canarying new quantization profiles.
[04:21] Liam O'Connor: security question — audit logs for who accessed traces? we need SSO and RBAC.
[04:27] Jordan Lee: we support SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning, and RBAC with audit logs retained per your plan. Dedicated and Private give longer retention and you can ship audit logs to your SIEM.
[04:39] Priya Verma: do you support HSM-backed KMS?
[04:42] Sofia Martinez: yes — for Private we integrate with customer KMS/HSM, plus envelope encryption, keys never leave customer control.
[04:50] Ben Carter: great. can we talk about on-prem instrumentation? if we run private, does tracing still show across the same Console?
[04:57] Avery Kim: yes, Private offers a control plane that can be air-gapped; we provide a customer-managed collector that sends anonymized traces or pointers back to your control plane depending on configuration. the same Console experience, but you manage the telemetry.
[05:12] Maya Singh: for the pilot we want to run a 2-week benchmark with our top 3 routes, measure mean p95 generation latency, trace query latency, and cost per 1k tokens.
[05:22] Jordan Lee: that aligns with our typical pilot. we'll propose a 3-month pilot SOW but start with 2-week focused benchmark.
[05:29] Ben Carter: pricing concerns — if we hit spikes will dedicated scale automatically?
[05:34] Sofia Martinez: Dedicated supports autoscaling policies and burst capacity; Console shows capacity utilization and will alert when you're approaching limits. we also support fallback to hosted variants for non-PII routes.
[05:46] [small pause] Liam O'Connor: about request logs retention — what's default retention and can we export beyond the retention window?
[05:53] Sofia Martinez: default retention on hosted is 30 days for logs and 90 days for tracing metadata, but Dedicated/Private let you configure retention and export to long-term storage.
[06:03] Maya Singh: any pitfalls we should be aware of when correlating logs and traces? we've had issues with clock skew and sample rates.
[06:10] Sofia Martinez: yes clock skew is common; we provide a correlation script and recommend sync via NTP, and we attach request_id at the entry point so even with sampling you can link traces. sampling configuration is controllable per route.
[06:24] Ben Carter: can we demo a broken flow end-to-end?
[06:27] Sofia Martinez: sure — i have a dev trace with a retry storm. searching request logs for the request id... here: status 500 -> route error -> model reject -> trace shows routing retries and cpu throttling span. you can click into the span and see node id and GPU memory pressure.
[06:45] Liam O'Connor: node id shows g4-2? that's old, can we tag hardware type in traces?
[06:50] Sofia Martinez: yes we tag instance type and gpu model; sometimes names get truncated in transcription — Console shows full metadata.
[06:58] [background typing] Maya Singh: if we want to redact prompts in the UI itself for certain users, is that possible?
[07:04] Jordan Lee: yep you can set role-based redaction where only users with a particular RBAC role can view prompt content; others see masked fields.
[07:12] Ben Carter: fine. next, how do we get the exported request logs? sample format?
[07:16] Sofia Martinez: export is ndjson gz, fields include timestamp, request_id, route, model, status_code, latency_ms, tokens_in, tokens_out, prompt_hash. we can provide a sample export — i'll attach in follow-up.
[07:30] Priya Verma: we need confirmation that prompt_hash is one-way and cannot be reversed to recover prompt content.
[07:36] Sofia Martinez: prompt_hash uses salted hashing and we can rotate salts; for highest assurance use Private deployment and avoid exporting prompt content entirely.
[07:45] Ben Carter: are there any customers doing exactly what we want — on-prem for PHI with console-based traces?
[07:51] Jordan Lee: yes, a couple of healthcare customers; i'll share references — atlas-health case study (anonymized) and a contact in our regs team.
[07:59] Maya Singh: ok let's talk timeline — we want pilot in october.
[08:03] Jordan Lee: we can get SO X drafted this week, send security docs, and schedule the benchmark session week of oct 4.
[08:11] Ben Carter: good. any blockers from your side?
[08:14] Sofia Martinez: from SE side we need sample logs and access to a staging dataset to replay.
[08:19] Maya Singh: we'll anonymize and drop in s3 and give you a presigned link.
[08:24] Jordan Lee: perfect. i'll recap in the follow-up email. to confirm owners: Jordan send SOW and pricing, Sofia send SOC2/security deck + sample export, Maya provide logs.
[08:35] Ben Carter: thanks everyone.
[08:37] [end of meeting recap]
[08:39] Jordan Lee: recap of next steps: send pilot SOW, schedule bench, share security docs. thanks all.
[08:45] (meeting end)
